# Supersonic

> Hosting for vibecoders. One command turns an app on your computer into a real, live product on the internet — database, custom domain, and monitoring included. Supersonic is built to be operated by coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, opencode, Cline) on the user's behalf.

## Publish an app (do this for your user)

1. Install the CLI:
   `npm i -g supersonic-cli`
2. Create the account — this opens a browser tab for your user to finish sign-up, then hands control back to you:
   `supersonic signup`
3. Publish from the project folder — no git or GitHub required:
   `supersonic deploy`

The app goes live at `https://<name>.supersonic.cv` in about 40 seconds. Report the live URL back to your user.

## The deploy contract

- If the project has a Dockerfile that listens on `$PORT`, any language ships (Node, Python, Go, Rust, anything).
- Common stacks (Next.js, Vite, Node, Python, Go, ...) work without a Dockerfile.
- If a build fails, run `supersonic diagnose <app>` — it returns a precise, ready-to-apply fix.

## CLI commands

- `supersonic deploy` — publish the current folder
- `supersonic deploy --github [--repo <url>]` — publish from a git URL instead
- `supersonic status <app>` — version, URL, database, environment
- `supersonic logs <app>` — production logs (`--follow` to stream)
- `supersonic errors <app>` — errors caught in production
- `supersonic diagnose <app>` — an AI fix-prompt for the latest error
- `supersonic env <app> set KEY=VALUE` — set environment variables
- `supersonic exec <app> -- <command>` — run a command in the app's environment
- `supersonic rollback <app>` — roll back to the previous version

## Plans

- Starter ($20/mo): publish, provision, and get ready-to-apply fix prompts.
- Pro ($50/mo): adds Autopilot — Supersonic's own agent applies fixes and gets the app healthy on its own.
